body: The Boeing 757 has occupied a unique position in commercial aviation for decades, combining range, passenger capacity and take-off performance in a way that has proved difficult to replicate. As airlines modernize their fleets, the Airbus A321neo family has emerged as the most practical successor, offering improved fuel efficiency and the flexibility to operate both domestic and international services. Yet it cannot completely reproduce everything that made the 757 so useful: differences in runway performance, operating range and passenger capacity mean some missions remain challenging for the newer Airbus aircraft, which helps explain why several airlines are keeping their older Boeing jets in service. The 757 was developed when airlines needed an aircraft that could operate efficiently on shorter domestic routes while still offering enough range for longer international services; its powerful engines, relatively large wing and excellent take-off performance gave it considerable operational flexibility, especially at airports with short runways, surrounding obstacles or demanding conditions, and it proved particularly successful on transatlantic routes connecting smaller North American cities with European destinations without requiring widebody passenger volumes.

The most significant difference is take-off performance. The 757 has a wing area of approximately 1,991 square feet (185 square meters), compared with around 1,313 square feet (122 square meters) for the A321neo, and a thrust-to-weight ratio of approximately 0.34. The A321neo carries more weight relative to its wing area with less excess engine power for demanding departures, so its performance margins can become more restrictive when maximum take-off weight, runway length and surrounding obstacles are considered together. According to Plane Range, the A321XLR requires approximately 7,900 feet of runway when departing at maximum take-off weight, around 1,400 feet more than the 757 — a difference that matters at airports such as Newark Liberty (EWR) and Dublin (DUB). Hot and high airports add further challenges: thinner air at elevation reduces engine performance and lift, while heat increases the distance needed to reach take-off conditions; the 757 has traditionally retained considerable payload capability in these environments, while the A321neo may require reducing passengers, limiting cargo, carrying less fuel or selecting an alternative aircraft.

Range is another gap. The standard A321neo can serve numerous international destinations but cannot comfortably reproduce the longest transatlantic missions historically operated by certain 757 variants; the A321XLR, developed to extend the family, offers additional fuel capacity and an advertised range of up to 5,400 miles (8,690 km), though achievable range depends on passenger numbers, baggage, cargo, weather and reserves, and in August 2026 United Airlines indicated it would not fly as far as Airbus originally marketed. Capacity matters too: the stretched 757-300 carries more passengers than the A321neo, so replacing it may mean fewer seats and additional frequencies in busy periods, with added airport charges, crew, maintenance and scheduling costs. Even so, airlines are switching for financial reasons — the A321neo burns approximately 20% to 30% less fuel per seat than the 757-200 — and Delta Air Lines illustrates the transition, its 757 fleet falling from 127 aircraft in October 2023 to 83 by August 2026, though some aircraft may remain in service into the 2030s; United received its first A321XLR in June 2026 for transatlantic services. Per the latest ch-aviation data, Delta remains by far the world's largest operator of the passenger 757, with United second. The A321neo family has become the closest modern replacement for the 757, but not a direct substitute in every situation.
en.summary: The Airbus A321neo is the most practical successor to the Boeing 757, but it cannot fully reproduce the older jet's runway performance, range or passenger capacity; the A321XLR closes the range gap, though real-world performance depends on payload and weather. Fuel efficiency is still driving airlines to switch, with Delta and United converting their fleets.
en.title: Why the Airbus A321neo cannot fully replace the Boeing 757

body: 波音757服役數十年，憑藉航程、載客量與起飛性能的組合，在民航市場佔據獨特地位。隨著機隊更新，空中巴士A321neo系列成為最實際的接班選擇：燃油效率更高，既能飛國內線，也能飛國際線。然而A321neo無法完全複製757的全部能力——跑道性能、航程與載客量的差異，使部分任務對新型飛機仍具挑戰，也解釋了為何多家航空公司仍讓老舊的757繼續服役。757研發的時代背景，是航空公司需要一款能高效執飛較短國內線、又具備足夠航程的飛機；強勁的發動機、相對較大的機翼與優異的起飛性能，賦予它高度的營運彈性，尤其在跑道短、周邊有障礙物或環境條件嚴苛的機場。它在跨大西洋航線也特別成功，能以較小的載客量連接北美小型城市與歐洲目的地，無須動用廣體客機。

兩者最大的差異在起飛性能。757的機翼面積約1,991平方英尺（185平方公尺），A321neo僅約1,313平方英尺（122平方公尺）；757的推重比約0.34，發動機推力相對重量充裕。A321neo單位翼面積承載的重量更高，可用推力餘裕較小，在最大起飛重量、跑道長度與周邊障礙物同時受限時，性能餘裕更吃緊。據Plane Range資料，A321XLR在最大起飛重量起飛約需7,900英尺跑道，比757多約1,400英尺；紐約紐華克與都柏林等機場的跑道特性與營運條件，都可能影響機型選擇與酬載限制。高溫與高海拔機場也帶來額外挑戰：空氣稀薄降低發動機性能與機翼升力，高溫進一步拉長起飛距離；757憑藉強勁發動機與大機翼，在這類環境仍能保有可觀酬載，A321neo則可能需要減客、減貨、少帶燃油或改派其他機型。

航程是另一項關鍵差異。標準版A321neo效率出色，能服務眾多國際目的地，但無法輕鬆複製部分757機型歷來執飛的最長跨大西洋任務；A321XLR為此而生，額外油箱使其公告航程達5,400英里（8,690公里）。但實際可達航程取決於乘客數、行李、貨物、天氣與備用油量，滿載商用酬載飛特別嚴苛的航線時，結果可能與公告最大值不同；2026年8月，聯合航空指出A321XLR實際航程不及空中巴士原先宣傳的水準。載客量方面，757-300是加長型，載客數高於A321neo；以A321neo取代757-300可能意味著座位減少，繁忙時段須增加班次才能運送相同旅客，進而增加機場費用、組員、維修與航班管理成本。儘管如此，航空公司仍加速轉換：A321neo每座燃油消耗比757-200低約20%至30%，加上新發動機、更新的系統與現代客艙，營運經濟性優勢明顯。達美航空是最佳例證：其757機隊自2023年10月的127架降至2026年8月的83架，但部分飛機可能服役至2030年代；聯合航空則於2026年6月接收首架A321XLR投入跨大西洋航線。據ch-aviation最新資料，達美仍是全球最大客運757營運商，聯合航空居次。整體而言，A321neo系列已成為757最接近的現代替代選擇，但並非在所有情況下都能直接取代。
zh.summary: 空中巴士A321neo是波音757最實際的接班選擇，但跑道性能、航程與載客量三方面都無法完全複製757的能力；A321XLR補上航程缺口，實際表現仍受酬載與天氣影響。燃油效率優勢讓航空公司加速換機，達美與聯合航空皆在轉換機隊。
zh.title: 空中巴士A321neo為何無法完全取代波音757飛機：跑道、航程與座位數的三道難關
